_readme: Real QS client webinar funnels, shown on the ROI Model tab beside the prospect's own projection. Every number is the client's actual recorded result from the workshop stats database — nothing modelled, nothing rounded up. Only clients whose Airtable row carries 'ROI Model' in 'Use on tabs' appear here. Source of truth: Airtable base appDBh76I8NAiE4l8, table Clients (tblGRxbKEYh9NoLqV). In production this is GET /api/jobs/:id/roi-comparisons and reads from Supabase.
_selection_rule: Use on tabs contains 'ROI Model' = complete invites/registrations/attendees/booked-calls recorded AND a confidence-6 TAM.
_shape_note: These clients' funnels record a REGISTRATION step that the prospect's projection does not model, and they stop at booked calls — no client has LTV or close-rate on file, so no dollar ROI can be shown for them. Display the funnel, never a revenue figure.
_matching: Alex's rule (2026-09-04 training, 1:07:33): lead with the client whose TAM is closest to the prospect's, regardless of what they sell.

examples.webinar_title: How Agencies Focus on Growth to 3X Client Retention & 2X Profitability
examples.why: ScaleTime is the closest analogue to DealForge's own prospects — operations consulting sold to agency owners — so a prospect in that world sees their exact buyer, not a loose parallel.

examples.webinar_title: Unlock Your Leadership Brilliance: Overcome People Challenges and Drive Results
examples.why: Lively Paradox is the proof that attendance rate, not list size, drives outcomes.

examples.webinar_title: Redefining the High-Volume Recruiting Process with AI and Automation
examples.why: GoHire is the clearest proof that the system scales: they went from 240 invites to 29,000+ per webinar across 18 runs and still held a 47% attendee-to-registrant rate at peak, which is the number most prospects assume collapses at volume.
